errorCodes.meaning: The supplied `cursor` cannot be honoured — expired, malformed, or issued against vault state no longer recognised. Consumers SHOULD retry from the first page without a cursor.

DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

EvidenceDocument.description: A whole Trust Task document — `id`, `type`, `payload` and every other member, `proof` included — carried exactly as it was sent or received, never re-serialised: a task digest and a proof are taken over its members, and a re-serialised copy reproduces neither reliably. Typed as an open object so every member survives; the checks that give it meaning belong to the task that reads it.
EvidenceDocument.title: EvidenceDocument

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

OutcomeEvidence.description: One witnessing session's outcome evidence. `session` is the initiating witness/session document; `outcome` is the terminal witness/session/submit #response that the initiating document's own specification declares as its outcome evidence, under the witness's proof, delivering the VWC and its vwcDigestMultibase. A consumer pairs them with a presented VWC by SPEC §4.9.4's four checks and the witnessing checks of witness/session/submit (This response is the outcome evidence).

outcome.description: The witness/session/submit #response that closed the session, under the witness's proof. It carries the VWC and its vwcDigestMultibase.

session.description: The witness/session document that opened the session. The VWC's taskContext is its id and its taskDigestMultibase is computed over it (SPEC §4.9.3).

OutcomeEvidence.title: OutcomeEvidence

Response.description: One entry per stored VWC that matched and that the caller may read. Empty when nothing matched, which is a successful answer, not an error.

nextCursor.description: Pass to the next request as `cursor` to continue. Present when the VTA stopped before the last match; absent when the page is the last. A consumer MUST NOT read a page carrying a `nextCursor` as a complete account of what is stored.

witnessings.description: The matching stored VWCs, each with its evidence.

Response.title: VTA Witness — List — response payload

StoredWitnessing.description: One VWC vta/witness/accept stored, as accept answered it, with the time it was stored. The VWC itself travels once, inside evidence.outcome, under the witness's proof.

credentialId.description: The credential-vault handle the VWC is stored under: the credentialId vta/witness/accept returned.

evidence.description: The outcome evidence stored with the VWC, each document exactly as stored, never re-serialised: `session`, the witness/session document as the VTA built it, and `outcome`, the witness/session/submit #response as received, which carries the VWC. Of whichever version the session was conducted under.

relationshipDid.description: The relationship DID the VWC names as its credentialSubject.id.

vwcDigestMultibase.description: The VWC's digest, as the witness returned it and the VTA checked it at accept: over the RFC 8785 canonicalization of the VWC, proof included.

witness.description: The witness that issued the VWC: its issuer, which is the recipient of evidence.session.

StoredWitnessing.title: StoredWitnessing

schema.description: A client reads back from its VTA the Verifiable Witness Credentials vta/witness/accept stored for its principal, each with the outcome evidence stored beside it. Every filter is optional and those present are AND-combined.

cursor.description: An opaque continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`; a responder MUST NOT accept a cursor it did not issue. Opaque: a consumer MUST NOT construct or parse one.

limit.description: The most entries to return; the responder chooses a default and MAY return fewer. The VTA caps this value.

relationshipDid.description: Only VWCs whose credentialSubject.id is this relationship DID.

witness.description: Only VWCs issued by this witness.

schema.title: VTA Witness — List — payload
